title: Delta detection and freeze record land as reusable primitives
description: User story under REQ-172. The detection-model foundation lands as pure, importable modules and one durable local record.
asA: the maintainer of a rcf-lite tree
iWant: hashDocument, computeTreeHash, computeDelta and the rcf/define/freeze.json reader/writer to land as pure modules exposed on the query surface, with a documented return shape that later DEFINE slices can call unchanged
soThat: the gates, readiness view, freeze verb and bundle-side read all consume the same detection primitives, and a hand reformat of a document never surfaces as a change

acceptanceCriteria.description: computeDelta(tree, freeze, ledgers) returns the exact object shape proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 2.2 specifies (frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, changed, added, removed, briefSince, unchanged); given a matching freeze the delta reports empty changed / added / removed and unchanged equal to the number of docHashes; given divergent tree state changed / added / removed classify every id correctly against the freeze record.

hashDocument returns a sha256:<64-hex> string over the canonical JSON form of the parsed document (keys sorted recursively, no whitespace), and is invariant under a whitespace-only reformat or a key reorder: two documents that parse to the same object hash identically.

Loading rcf/define/freeze.json when the file is absent returns null; loading a malformed file (bad JSON, missing docHashes, non-sha256 hash value, negative briefStatements) raises FreezeRecordError with a code (parseFailure or schemaFailure) and a named field so a caller can log the exact failure.

Saving then loading a freeze record round-trips every documented field including extension fields the schema does not police (counts, litmus, versions, note), and saveFreezeRecord refuses to persist an invalid record: no file is written on validation failure.
